Looking at the data:

| Capacity (MW) | Completion Year |
|---------------|-----------------|
| 44            | 2011            |
| 45            | 2011            |
| 160           | 2011            |
| 240           | 2011            |
| 330           | 2016            |
| 520           | 2012            |
| 800           | 2013            |
| 2000          | 2014            |

Calculating correlation: The data shows no consistent pattern. Four plants with capacities ranging from 44-240 MW were all completed in 2011, suggesting no capacity-related delay. The 330 MW plant (2016) completed later than the 2000 MW plant (2014), which contradicts any capacity-driven timeline. The correlation coefficient is approximately 0.38, indicating a weak relationship that is not statistically significant given the small sample size and counterexamples.

Final Answer: No, there is no meaningful causal relationship between total capacity and completion schedule. The correlation coefficient is weak (approximately 0.38), and multiple counterexamples exist—the 330 MW plant completed in 2016 while the much larger 2000 MW plant completed earlier in 2014, and four plants with vastly different capacities (44-240 MW) all completed in the same year.
